---
title: "GT Integration Demo"
html-table-processing: none
---

The whole pipeline: a table made with [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/)
in Python, turned into gridwell IR, and rendered by gridwell's writers.

## Python code

```python
from great_tables import GT, exibble
import gridwell

gt = (
    GT(
        exibble[["row", "group", "char", "num", "currency"]],
        rowname_col="row",
        groupname_col="group",
        id="groups_and_stub",
    )
    .fmt_number(columns="num", decimals=2)
    .fmt_currency(columns="currency", currency="USD")
)

table = gridwell.Table(gt)    # the table as gridwell IR
assert table.validate() == []
print(table.render("latex"))
```

This is the `groups_and_stub` case of the [conformance kit](https://github.com/rich-iannone/gridwell/tree/main/conformance),
and the IR below is the one checked in for it, which the Python tests keep current.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}

## Outputs

Every tab but "Great Tables" is the real output of `gridwell convert` for that IR,
which the docs' tests check. "Great Tables" is Great Tables' own HTML for the same
table (`as_raw_html()`), to compare with gridwell's Preview. The HTML tab shows the
markup without the base stylesheet (`"base_styles": false`); the ANSI tab is drawn
without color.

::: {.panel-tabset}
